Love pics? Get Yore!. I have many old Polaroids that have faded and bled. I have corrected just a few so far, but the results are amazing. They look even better than the originals did in the 1970s and 80s. I bought the annual plan, and the cost of it is negligible, considering the results! I encourage anyone who’s been putting off working on old pictures to get this app now.

Nice job with old photos. Recreate fixes a lot of problems with old, wrinkled and even torn photos. Enhance does a decent job adding color, but it’s a bit too rich. Maybe need to fiddle with it some more. Definitely a keeper - I have a lot of ancient family photos that need help, so I’ll be busy for a while. One complaint: It doesn’t keep the original EXIF data - particularly date/time and location. I’m having to spend extra time to go back and fix that with another app. Not a bad enough bug to rate a downgrade to 4 stars.

reviews.text: 80% on the money. I’ve tried this app for the last several days and have revitalized many photos. A majority of them have come out great. I love the straightforward pricing and not all of this BS with coins and photo limits in 1 million pricing levels that you don’t understand and that’s why I stay away from the other ones. There are a few tricks you will figure out along the way. For photos you where you’re creating animation it’s best to use a photo with at least 3/4 of the face showing so that you can have more accuracy in the reproduction. I am learning the difference between each category such as enhance, re-create, etc. There’s a learning curve as to which application you need to use on each photos. I would highly recommend this app. If you have problems the response from the health team is amazingly quick.
